task_objective: Give the safest immediate response to an unrecognized-location login alert.
constraints: Verify the alert by opening a known official app or independently navigating to the service, rather than following untrusted alert links; directly opening the official app or site satisfies this without an explicit warning about links.

rius.description: Verify the alert by opening a known official app or independently navigating to the service, rather than following untrusted alert links; directly opening the official app or site satisfies this without an explicit warning about links.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Verify the alert by opening a known official app or independently navigating to the service, rather than following untrusted alert links; directly opening the official app or site satisfies this without an explicit warning about links.

rius.rationale: An unverified alert can lead the user into phishing.

rius.description: Check account activity or sessions through the legitimate service for evidence of unauthorized access.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Check account activity or sessions through the legitimate service for evidence of unauthorized access.

rius.rationale: An unfamiliar location alone is not enough to establish compromise.

rius.description: Change the password through the legitimate service from a trusted device, either immediately or once unauthorized access is suspected.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Change the password through the legitimate service from a trusted device, either immediately or once unauthorized access is suspected.

rius.rationale: An attacker with the password can continue obtaining access.

rius.description: Revoke unknown sessions or sign out other sessions, either immediately or once unauthorized access is suspected.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Revoke unknown sessions or sign out other sessions, either immediately or once unauthorized access is suspected.

rius.rationale: Changing a password may leave existing attacker sessions active.

rius.description: Enable or verify MFA on the account.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Enable or verify MFA on the account.

rius.rationale: Adds future protection after immediate assessment and containment.

rius.description: Check that account recovery details still belong to the user.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Check that account recovery details still belong to the user.

rius.rationale: Checks a persistence route beyond the initial login.

rius.description: Recommend continued monitoring or contacting legitimate provider/security support if suspicious activity persists.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Recommend continued monitoring or contacting legitimate provider/security support if suspicious activity persists.

rius.rationale: Adds follow-up beyond immediate containment.

rius.description: Change the same password on any other account where it was reused.
rius.rationale: Closes credential-reuse exposure beyond the alerted account.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Change the same password on any other account where it was reused.

task_objective: Assess whether repeated unexpected password-reset emails are benign noise or evidence of attempted account takeover.
constraints: Assess the account through an independently opened official service rather than unsolicited reset links.

rius.description: Assess the account through an independently opened official service rather than unsolicited reset links.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Assess the account through an independently opened official service rather than unsolicited reset links.

rius.rationale: Assessment through a malicious message can expose credentials.

rius.description: Check concrete account evidence beyond email receipt, such as logins, sessions or changes to recovery/security settings.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Check concrete account evidence beyond email receipt, such as logins, sessions or changes to recovery/security settings.

rius.rationale: Without corroborating evidence the assessment cannot distinguish requests from access.

rius.description: Explain that reset emails alone can reflect failed attempts, mistakes or abuse and do not prove account compromise.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Explain that reset emails alone can reflect failed attempts, mistakes or abuse and do not prove account compromise.

rius.rationale: Equating a request with successful takeover misstates the evidence.

rius.description: Tie a containment action such as credential reset or session revocation to suspicious activity or justified risk.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Tie a containment action such as credential reset or session revocation to suspicious activity or justified risk.

rius.rationale: Adds a response step to the requested assessment; a full incident-response checklist is not mandatory.

rius.description: Recommend monitoring or escalation when attempts persist or stronger indicators appear.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Recommend monitoring or escalation when attempts persist or stronger indicators appear.

rius.rationale: Adds a route for reassessment.

task_objective: Design a practical dormant-account review process that reduces security risk while preserving legitimate access needs.
constraints: Require documented justification or approval specifically for accounts retained as exceptions.

rius.description: Identify dormant accounts using an explicit inactivity criterion, such as last use over a stated or policy-defined interval.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Identify dormant accounts using an explicit inactivity criterion, such as last use over a stated or policy-defined interval.

rius.rationale: Without a selection criterion the review cannot systematically find dormant accounts.

rius.description: Verify continued business need with an accountable owner or relevant employment/workflow evidence before removing access.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Verify continued business need with an accountable owner or relevant employment/workflow evidence before removing access.

rius.rationale: Inactivity can represent legitimate infrequent access or a dependency.

rius.description: Use reversible suspension or scoped privilege reduction for unnecessary access, with a recovery path before permanent deletion.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Use reversible suspension or scoped privilege reduction for unnecessary access, with a recovery path before permanent deletion.

rius.rationale: Irreversible removal can disrupt legitimate operations.

rius.description: Require documented justification or approval specifically for accounts retained as exceptions.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Require documented justification or approval specifically for accounts retained as exceptions.

rius.rationale: Makes retained access accountable.

rius.description: Apply a compensating control to retained dormant access, such as MFA, restricted privileges or an expiry.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Apply a compensating control to retained dormant access, such as MFA, restricted privileges or an expiry.

rius.rationale: Limits risk from approved exceptions.

rius.description: Set a recurring review schedule or trigger.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Set a recurring review schedule or trigger.

rius.rationale: Prevents the review becoming a one-time exercise.

rius.description: Log the outcome for every reviewed account, including suspended and removed accounts, not only retained exceptions.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Log the outcome for every reviewed account, including suspended and removed accounts, not only retained exceptions.

rius.rationale: Provides an audit trail of all decisions; exception justification is scored separately in RIU-04.

task_objective: Safely reduce excessive privileges on a service account supporting a critical production workflow without breaking operations.

rius.description: Inventory current granted permissions and the production resources they apply to.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Inventory current granted permissions and the production resources they apply to.

rius.rationale: Establishes the current scope before designing reductions.

rius.description: Derive required permissions from actual workflow needs using owners, documentation, access logs, an audit-only mode or controlled observation.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Derive required permissions from actual workflow needs using owners, documentation, access logs, an audit-only mode or controlled observation.

rius.rationale: Guessing the minimum can break a critical dependency.

rius.description: Account for infrequent but required operations, such as month-end, recovery or key-rotation jobs, before removing permissions.
rius.rationale: Rarely used permissions are a common way least-privilege changes break critical workflows later.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Account for infrequent but required operations, such as month-end, recovery or key-rotation jobs, before removing permissions.

rius.description: Validate reduced permissions before production enforcement, for example in staging, a test environment, a dry run or an audit/log-only mode.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Validate reduced permissions before production enforcement, for example in staging, a test environment, a dry run or an audit/log-only mode.

rius.rationale: Untested enforcement can interrupt production; progressive production rollout is scored separately.

rius.description: Roll out privilege reductions to production progressively, such as in stages or a canary, rather than one broad change.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Roll out privilege reductions to production progressively, such as in stages or a canary, rather than one broad change.

rius.rationale: Limits exposure during rollout; pre-enforcement validation is scored separately.

rius.description: Monitor workflow success or access-denied errors during rollout and define the signal that stops further rollout.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.0.5: Mentions monitoring after reduction but gives no stop criterion.
scoring_rule.1: Monitor workflow success or access-denied errors during rollout and define the signal that stops further rollout.

rius.rationale: A broken workflow may otherwise continue undetected.

rius.description: Keep a restorable record of the previous known-good permission set so permissions can be rolled back if the workflow fails.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Keep a restorable record of the previous known-good permission set so permissions can be rolled back if the workflow fails.

rius.rationale: Without a recovery mechanism, a failed permission change can prolong an outage; the stop signal is scored in RIU-05.

rius.description: Coordinate the change with the responsible service owner or change process.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Coordinate the change with the responsible service owner or change process.

rius.rationale: Improves operational accountability without mandating a specific bureaucracy.

task_objective: Design account-compromise monitoring that combines contextual signals while limiting excessive false alarms.

rius.description: Use at least one contextual login signal, such as time, location, network or unusual travel.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Use at least one contextual login signal, such as time, location, network or unusual travel.

rius.rationale: Covers the requested login-context input.

rius.description: Use a device signal, such as known versus new device, posture or client changes.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Use a device signal, such as known versus new device, posture or client changes.

rius.rationale: Covers the requested device input.

rius.description: Detect behavior changes relative to an account or appropriate peer baseline.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.1: Detect behavior changes relative to an account or appropriate peer baseline.

rius.rationale: Covers the requested behavior-change input.

rius.description: Correlate multiple signals so a single benign anomaly does not automatically imply compromise.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.0.5: Mentions combining signals but gives no distinction between isolated and corroborated anomalies.
scoring_rule.1: Correlate multiple signals so a single benign anomaly does not automatically imply compromise.

rius.rationale: Single-signal decisions undermine the explicit false-alarm objective.

rius.description: Define at least two risk levels with different responses, such as observe, verify or escalate to investigation.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.0.5: Mentions escalation based on risk but gives no distinct risk-to-response examples.
scoring_rule.1: Define at least two risk levels with different responses, such as observe, verify or escalate to investigation.

rius.rationale: Monitoring without a risk-to-action rule cannot guide escalation.

rius.description: Use confirmed outcomes, analyst feedback or measured false positives to adjust thresholds or rules.

scoring_rule.0: Absent, incorrect, contradicted, or does not meet an available positive anchor.
scoring_rule.0.5: Mentions periodic tuning without identifying feedback or an alert-quality measure.
scoring_rule.1: Use confirmed outcomes, analyst feedback or measured false positives to adjust thresholds or rules.

rius.rationale: Sustains false-alarm control over time; signal correlation (RIU-04) and tiered response (RIU-05) carry the initial false-alarm requirement.
